assumptions.rationale: June 30 2026 balance: cash & equivalents $2.503B, short-term investments $2.161B, long-term investments $4.116B (high-grade marketable securities, no haircut). Debt $7.631B = short-term $2.196B (mostly ~$2.1B commercial paper under the $3B CP program) + long-term $5.435B (2030 notes $1.5B + $4.0B notes issued to repay the Armis term loan). Operating/finance lease obligations ($0.94B) are treated in cash costs, not debt. Cross-check: $1.5B + $4.0B + ~$2.1B CP ≈ $7.6B.
assumptions.falsifier: Primary 10-Q balance sheet shows debt or cash differing by more than $250M from these figures.

assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time common shares 1,033,862,000 (10-Q cover count via AV overview; post 5-for-1 split basis). Q1 ASR retired 18.5M shares.
assumptions.falsifier: 10-Q cover count differs by more than 0.5%.

assumptions.rationale: Add 5M shares for vested in-the-money options/settling awards. Unvested RSUs are NOT added: all future equity awards are charged as a cash-equivalent cost (sbc_policy=cash_equivalent), so adding unvested RSUs would double count.
assumptions.falsifier: Diluted-share disclosure shows options/vested awards above 15M.

assumptions.rationale: No preferred stock or material noncontrolling interests. Deferred revenue renews in a going concern and is modeled as a ledger (not free profit and not a runoff claim). No contingent consideration of material size identified in available excerpts.
assumptions.falsifier: Filing discloses material contingent consideration, preferred claims or minority interests.

assumptions.rationale: Bridge June 30 -> Sep 28: explicit estimate of NO net change. Q3 is seasonally weak for operating cash (Q3 2025 OCF $0.81B) and the company continues buybacks under the $5B authorization plus possible CP paydown; these roughly offset. No acquisition closing of material size since June 30 was found. Not verified until the Q3 10-Q (late October).
assumptions.falsifier: Q3 2026 10-Q shows net cash+investments minus debt changed by more than $1B, or share count by more than 1%.

assumptions.rationale: Opening deferred revenue estimated at $7.0B (AV lacks the line; ~43% of annual revenue, consistent with annual upfront billing; revenue recognized from opening deferred was $3.4B in Q2). Balance kept at 43% of annual revenue so growth funds working capital. Timing effect only; small value impact.
assumptions.falsifier: Filed deferred revenue differs from $7.0B by more than $1.5B.

assumptions.rationale: FY26 subscription revenue guidance $15.76-15.78B (+22.5%, incl. ~125bp Armis) + ~$0.42B services => ~$16.19B total; H1 actual $7.757B, so Q4 ~$4.29B. Stub 2026-09-28..12-31 (~94 days) revenue ~$4.38B = $17.0B annual rate.
assumptions.falsifier: Q3/Q4 revenue below $4.0B/$4.15B or guidance cut.

assumptions.rationale: Base: 2027 +18% (matches ~$19.1B consensus), then fade 16.5/15/13.5/12/10.5/9/7.5/6% through 2035. Outside view: few $15B+ software firms sustain >15% for 5 years; NOW has compounded 21-24% for 5 years with cRPO +21.5% cc and $29.0B RPO, supporting a gradual fade rather than a cliff.
assumptions.falsifier: cRPO constant-currency growth below 15% for two consecutive quarters.

assumptions.rationale: Bear: AI agents compress seat-based workflow pricing and IT budgets shift to model vendors/hyperscalers; growth 14% in 2027 fading to 4% by 2035. This is a structural-disruption case, not a recession-only dip.
assumptions.falsifier: Net new ACV and seat expansion stay above +18% through 2027 with stable pricing.

assumptions.rationale: Bull: AI ACV ($1B+ in Q2, targeting $1.5B end-2026) plus Armis/security and CRM expansion keep growth ~19-20% through 2029, fading to 7% by 2035.
assumptions.falsifier: AI ACV below $1.5B at end-2026 or AI SKUs cannibalize core seats.

assumptions.rationale: Cash cost ratio (excluding SBC and D&A) 66% in the Q4-2026 stub (FY25 EBITDA before SBC = 34.0% of revenue: 1824+1955+738; 2026 burdened by Armis integration), 64.5% in 2027 (EBITDA before SBC 35.5% less 4.5% depreciation ~ FY26 non-GAAP margin guide of 31.5%), falling to 58% by 2035 as scale and AI automation lift efficiency. Implied reported FCF margin ~34-35% in 2026-27 matches FY26 guidance of 35%.
assumptions.falsifier: Non-GAAP operating margin falls below 30% in FY27.

assumptions.rationale: Bear: AI inference costs and price competition keep cash costs at 63-66% of revenue (EBITDA before SBC ~37% by 2035); SBC stays above 10% of revenue.
assumptions.falsifier: Subscription gross margin and operating margin expand despite AI mix.

assumptions.rationale: Bull: operating leverage takes cash costs to 56% (EBITDA before SBC 44%) by 2035 and SBC falls to 7.5% of revenue.
assumptions.falsifier: Operating margin stalls near 31% non-GAAP through 2028.

assumptions.rationale: SBC 14.7% of revenue in FY25 (~$1.96B), elevated to ~15.5% in 2026 by Armis retention awards (Q2 $652M). Management targets SBC below 10% of revenue by 2029. Base follows the target by 2030, bear misses it, bull beats it. SBC charged as cash-equivalent cost (economically equal to buybacks offsetting dilution).
assumptions.falsifier: FY27 SBC above 14% of revenue.

assumptions.rationale: Depreciation of PP&E ~4.5% of revenue plus amortization of acquired intangibles ($3.78B on balance after Armis) running off: ~$560M in 2027 (~$150M in the Q4 2026 stub; Q2 2026 total D&A $407M) falling to ~$50M by 2035. Capex (incl. data centers) 4.5% of revenue through 2028, 4.3% thereafter (FY25 6.5%, H1 2026 ~3.3%; midpoint allows for AI infrastructure).
assumptions.falsifier: Capex exceeds 7% of revenue for AI infrastructure for two years.

assumptions.rationale: Recurring tuck-in acquisitions cost 1.5% of revenue per year (Moveworks, Armis, Veza show acquisitions are part of the model). Charged as growth capex so acquired growth is not free.
assumptions.falsifier: A further acquisition above $5B is announced.

assumptions.rationale: Cash tax 20% of taxable operating income after SBC deduction and interest; terminal 21%. FY25 effective tax ~23% on pretax $2.26B.
assumptions.falsifier: Cash taxes exceed 25% of pretax income for two years.

assumptions.rationale: Debt held flat at $7.63B: commercial paper (~$2.1B) rolls under the $3B program and notes are refinanced at maturity (repaying CP from cash would be value-neutral apart from the interest spread). Blended rate 4.1% (2030 notes 1.4%, new notes 4.25-6.3%, CP ~4.3%) through 2030, 5.1% thereafter after refinancing the low-coupon 2030 notes.
assumptions.falsifier: Credit rating downgrade or refinancing above 6.5%.

assumptions.rationale: Marketable investments $6.28B earn ~3.5% pre-tax, 21% tax => ~$174M/yr after tax; principal kept and counted once in the terminal bridge.
assumptions.falsifier: Investments liquidated for acquisitions or buybacks.

assumptions.rationale: Excess cash above $1.5B minimum is returned (modeled as a distribution; economically equivalent to buybacks at fair value, as with the $2.0B Q1 ASR).
assumptions.falsifier: Cash is instead accumulated or spent on value-destroying acquisitions.

assumptions.rationale: Cost of equity 9.75% = 10y UST 4.99% + beta 0.97 x ERP ~4.9%. Terminal WACC 9.5% (debt ~5% of capital at ~4% after tax). Same rate in all scenarios so scenarios differ by business outcomes only.
assumptions.falsifier: Long rates move by more than 1 point.

assumptions.rationale: Base terminal after 2035: growth 3%, operating margin 29.5% INCLUDING SBC (2035 explicit ~29.6%), ROIC 25% (asset-light software incl. acquired goodwill).
assumptions.falsifier: Mature GAAP margin including SBC stays below 25%.

assumptions.rationale: Bear terminal: growth 2.5%, margin 22.5% incl. SBC, ROIC 15% (commoditized workflow software).
assumptions.falsifier: Retention and pricing hold through the AI transition.

assumptions.rationale: Bull terminal: growth 3.5%, margin 32% incl. SBC, ROIC 35% (platform control point for enterprise AI agents).
assumptions.falsifier: Margins plateau below 30% or competition caps ROIC.

assumptions.rationale: Competitive response: stock fell ~57% from $192.6 high to $81.25 low within 52 weeks on fears that AI agents (model vendors, Salesforce/Microsoft agents) erode seat-based workflow software. Offsetting evidence: 24% revenue growth, cRPO +21.5% cc, AI ACV > $1B. Bear case prices in structural pressure.
assumptions.falsifier: Churn/renewal rate falls below 97% or price realization declines.

assumptions.rationale: FY2027 revenue consensus $19.16B (web excerpts, Sep 21 2026); GAAP basis revenue equals model basis. Adjusted EPS consensus excludes SBC and amortization, so it is not compared to the model EPS proxy.
assumptions.falsifier: Refreshed consensus differs by more than 5%.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.thesis: AI agents structurally pressure seat-based pricing; growth slows to mid-single digits and margins stall.

terminal.working_capital_rationale: Deferred revenue renews with subscriptions in a going concern; growth in the balance is funded by the g/ROIC reinvestment rule. No runoff claim.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.thesis: Durable enterprise workflow platform; growth fades from ~18% to 6% by 2035 while margins expand and SBC falls toward management target.

terminal.working_capital_rationale: Deferred revenue renews with subscriptions in a going concern; growth in the balance is funded by the g/ROIC reinvestment rule. No runoff claim.

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.thesis: NOW becomes the enterprise AI-agent control layer; ~20% growth persists to 2029 with strong operating leverage.

terminal.working_capital_rationale: Deferred revenue renews with subscriptions in a going concern; growth in the balance is funded by the g/ROIC reinvestment rule. No runoff claim.

note: Real regression input from the 2026-09-28 ServiceNow run (Claude Code cloud session). Balances via Alpha Vantage and search excerpts; primary filings NOT read directly (egress blocked), hence retrieval labels. Not a price target; rerun in Cowork after reading the 10-Q.
